title: Detuning-assisted cavity enhancement in spectroscopy
authors: Subhasish Guha, Sourav Das, Francesco Albarelli, Aiman Khan, Elnaz Darsheshdar, Adam D. Wright, Animesh Datta
abstract: Cavity-enhanced spectroscopy is a widely used experimental technique. We show that detuning the cavity frequency from the transition of interest can enhance the precision for dipole moment estimation by up to two orders of magnitude beyond the improvement when the cavity is resonant with the transition. We show this for both classical continuous-wave (CW) and pulsed single-photon probes, even in the presence of losses. We trace this enhancement to a detuning-controlled redistribution of information between the light- and matter-like polaritons, with losses determining the optimal branch. We show that this enhancement remains accessible using conventional photodetection and time-correlated single-photon counting.
summary: This paper theoretically investigates cavity-enhanced spectroscopy, proving that detuning the cavity frequency from the atomic transition can dramatically boost measurement precision. The enhancement, termed Detuning-Assisted Enhancement, is quantified using both classical and quantum Fisher Information metrics. It shows this technique is robust and applicable using standard detection methods.
main_problem: To demonstrate that detuning the cavity frequency from the atomic transition can significantly enhance the precision of dipole moment estimation in cavity-enhanced spectroscopy (CES).
main_result: Detuning-Assisted Enhancement (DAE) boosts estimation precision by up to two orders of magnitude compared to the resonant case, applicable to both classical and single-photon probes.
method: The study employs both semiclassical (Fisher Information) and fully quantum (Quantum Fisher Information) approaches to quantify the enhancement.
model_or_system: The system models a Two-Level Atom (TLA) coupled to a Fabry-Perot cavity, analyzed under both continuous-wave (CW) and pulsed single-photon probing conditions.
key_observables: Fisher Information (FI) and Quantum Fisher Information (QFI) for dipole moment estimation.
important_parameters: Detunings ($\Delta_C, \Delta_{AC}$), cavity loss rate ($K$), atomic loss rate ($\Gamma$), and coupling strength ($g$).
main_assumptions: The analysis uses the transfer matrix method and assumes the TLA can be mapped to effective single-atom models for ensembles.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate transmission spectra and dimensionless FI/QFI plots, comparing resonant vs. detuned conditions for both CW and pulsed probes.
paper_structure: The paper systematically develops the theoretical framework for CES, first addressing the semiclassical CW limit, then moving to the fully quantum single-photon regime, and finally quantifying the enhancement using FI and QFI.
why_interesting: This work provides quantitative, rigorous bounds on measurement precision in a fundamental quantum optics setup (cavity QED), showing how detuning can be a powerful tool to overcome limitations inherent at resonance.

figures.caption: Figure 1. Schematic of cavity-enhanced spectroscopy, showing the two types of light probes we consider. In typical mod- els for spectroscopy, continuous-wave monochromatic light probes (a) are considered, and the output light amplitude is modified according to the transmission of the sample. For pulsed single photon probes (b), the sample modifies the shape of the input pulse. K represents the strength of coupling between the input probe light and the cavity mode, whereas g is the interaction strength between the cavity and the two- level atom (TLA). Γ and K⊥represent the losses from the atom and the cavity into the continuum respectively.

Figure 2. Transmission spectra T (ω)(top panels) and the dimensionless FI (bottom panels) of photodetection for CEAS including atomic loss (a) Γ = g/100 and (b) Γ = g are plotted against the detuning between the input probe frequency ωin and the cavity frequency, with solid blue and black lines respectively. The dashed blue lines represent the polariton frequencies ϵ±, while the green dash dotted lines and red dotted lines represent the bare frequencies of the cavity and atom respectively. We set K = g/2, K⊥= 0, g = 3.3 × 10−4cm−1 ≈10MHz in these plots.
